classification: retained public column-bracket bounds defect; current small generator populations are not claimed affected
title: Reject rounded out-of-range column indices before forming their successor
contract_trace: SurfaceColumn::at accepts any u32 and stores column as f32. at(u32::MAX) rounds to2^32. In bracket(u32::MAX), (columns-1) as f32 rounds to the same2^32, so the upper-bound check accepts it. The float-to-u32 conversion then saturates first to MAX and first+1 overflows with overflow checks; otherwise the returned first is still outside the population and the successor wraps. The public helper therefore fails its own Option-based bounds contract for admitted inputs without requiring any allocation. Current garment/chart callers use much smaller populations, so no existing visible armor failure from this witness is asserted.
repair: Establish exact contextual column/population bounds at source admission and recheck the converted first index against columns before forming the successor. Reject invalid projected coordinates through the owning fallible contract, and ensure every Some bracket has first<=second<columns and finite legal interpolation. Reuse agreed contextual count/index owners, preserve valid native f32 arithmetic/rounding and fractional cut coordinates, and trace all SurfaceColumn/Grid consumers. Do not invent a global design population cap or merely saturate the successor while leaving first outside the population. Broader ordinal/fraction precision and interpolation admission remain PC30 until traced.

classification: retained native-format extent admission gap; no ordinary export reaching the limit asserted
title: Admit binary glTF container extents before narrowing them into headers
contract_trace: The GLB encoder receives actual serialized JSON and binary payload byte vectors, rounds both lengths up to four-byte alignment, sums the header/chunk extents as usize and writes total_length/json_bytes.len()/bytes.len() with unchecked as u32 casts. Native u32 words are the real format boundary, but neither alignment/sum overflow nor representability of each chunk and complete container is established before those projections. A sufficiently large admitted payload can therefore produce a truncated header or overflow the host arithmetic instead of an owning error. Current bounded ordinary MHR exports have not been proved to reach this limit; no huge allocation or file was created in this audit.
repair: At the actual encoder boundary, admit one checked GLB layout covering padding, both chunk extents and the complete container, and reject host arithmetic or native32-bit representation failure before resizing/copying/writing. Keep checked lengths through the shared layout/encoder; emit raw u32 only when writing header words. Use a focused native-format layout/error contract rather than a naked cast or arbitrary smaller global export cap. Reuse byte-unit concepts where semantics fit, but do not equate this format32-bit limit with GPU buffer/device or word-count contracts. Propagate failure through the owning structured export error M20.
